Risk officer assessment for AOR:

Refuse. Do not buy at any size.

Reasons from the brief: the class is OPERATOR, but the curve data looks like a single controller: bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, with the top 5 buyers holding 99.9% of early buys. Early buy volume of 682.88 SOL ex-agent came from 17 buyers, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes was 0.0005, meaning almost nothing was sold. That is the signature of a supply concentrated in insiders, not a market.

Recent action is thin: last 15 minutes show about $2,020 volume against a $4.08M market cap, with 30 sellers versus 41 buyers. The 83x 30-minute return is a launch artifact, and the price sits 0.02% off its high, so the next exit depends entirely on the operator's willingness to sell into a 780 SOL pool. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% plus impact would be large relative to any realistic exit.

I would size zero. The name ("American Oil Reserve") is creator-chosen and carries no information. Revisit only if the bundle concentration falls and sell-side depth appears.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying AOR now is weak, and I don't think it clears the bar.

The strongest point in the brief is real momentum: the coin is up about 83x over 30 minutes, it's still alive, and the last 15 minutes show net inflow of 1.2 SOL with 41 buyers against 30 sellers. Drawdown from the 30-minute high is nearly zero, so it hasn't started to fade.

But the structure argues against demand being durable. The first two minutes after graduation saw 683 SOL bought ex-agent, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.9% of volume and a bundle share of 1.0. That is classic operator concentration, and the curve metrics show one or three wallets doing essentially all the buying. The last 15 minutes are also thin: 9 SOL bought against 8 SOL sold, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0005 at launch shows nothing was sold into early. Demand that depends on a handful of wallets doesn't persist once they stop.

I'd recommend skipping. Operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even, and this one sits at a 4M market cap with a 780 SOL pool, so a $20 round trip paying 1.4 to 5.1% in fees and impact has little room. Nothing in the brief shows broad buyers who will still be there in 30 to 60 minutes.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is insider distribution into a thin book. The curve data is extreme: bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0 mean the bundled wallets hold effectively all supply, and top5_buyer_share of 0.999 with sell_to_buy_ratio of 0.0005 in the first two minutes shows the launch buyers accumulated and have not sold yet, which is what precedes a dump. completer_share of 2.87 and a launch_bot_present flag point to coordinated operator activity, not organic demand. The last 15 minutes are a warning: sell_sol of 7.95 against buy_sol of 9.15, with 30 sellers versus 41 buyers, net flow of only 1.2 SOL, and a 0.28% return on $2,020 volume. Price is up 83x in 30 minutes but has barely moved recently. A $20 ticket on a 1.4-5.1% round trip only needs a small reversal to lose. Skip.
